text:
ana: FYI posted the Equinox postmortem actions here -> https://rwd.infra/pm/INF-4321 :link: Please skim and claim owners for the remediation items by EOD tomorrow.

matt: reading now. quick note — the isolation bug looks like it only surfaced under BGP failover in their colo. I can own the network-facing follow-ups.

jas: I can take the on-prem infra work (container network namespace cleanup + firewall rules audit). ETA 2w? need confirmation on access windows from Equinox.

ana: @ana -> typo, but use "ana"? (just a reaction) :smile:

sophia: tagging infra-sre: we should schedule a canary for dedicated capacity after fixes. i'll draft the canary plan and post by friday.

kevin: noted. I'll open an RFC for updating the peering runbook to cover the BGP flaps scenario and include explicit rollback steps. RFC id: RFC-287. target review in 3 business days.

matt: action items I'm taking:
- INF-4321-1: validate BGP timers + graceful restart config on Equinox edge (owner: matt, due: 1901340000)
- INF-4321-2: add BGP monitoring alert (owner: matt, due: 1901300000)

jas: my tasks:
- INF-4321-3: container network namespace GC script + cron (owner: jas, due: 1901880000)
- INF-4321-4: firewall rule phantom-check (owner: jas, due: 1902000000)

ana: sophia + kevin — can you two coordinate the canary gating criteria? we want latency SLOs + isolation regression tests (simple prompts to exercise peering failover).

sophia: yes — proposed gating: 99th percentile token latency within 15% of baseline, no more than 0.2% error rate for 2 consecutive 30m windows. will add regression prompts to the eval suite.

kevin: added runbook checklist items:
```
- pre-check: collect route tables + BGP summary
- during: enable verbose peering logs
- post: validate session persistence & token-level traces
```
I'll attach to RFC-287.

ana: @matt @jas please paste any access commands or ephemeral creds in #eng-security when needed — do NOT paste in this thread.

matt: ack. requesting Equinox for a maintenance window Tues 01:00-03:00 UTC.

jas: noted. will schedule GC deploy into that window. prepping a small rollback image just in case.

deploy-bot: Scheduled weekly follow-up thread created: thread_ts=1901238000, cadence=weekly, owner=@ana. First check-in: 1901840000.

ana: thanks all. one pattern callout from the postmortem: several of these customer isolation issues trace back to intermittent on-prem switch firmware + aggressive BFD timers. ops-recommendation: we should start tracking vendor/firmware across Dedicated customers and include that in customer health dashboards. can someone own an initial inventory?

kevin: I can take inventory ownership. will spin up a lightweight spreadsheet and aim to backfill top 20 Dedicated customers in 1 sprint. JIRA: INF-4321-INV.

matt: quick troubleshooting snippet for reference (from the incident):
```
# show bgp summary
Neighbor        V    AS MsgRcv MsgSent  TblVer  InQ OutQ Up/Down  State/PfxRcd
10.0.0.1        4 65001  12345  12350       0    0    0 02:13:22        0
```
Look for flaps correlated with BFD logs.

jas: also saw a kernel oops on the node during failover. filing INF-4321-KO for kernel followup.

ana: OK, we have owners and immediate due dates. I'll consolidate into the postmortem doc and update INF-4321 with sub-tasks. We'll re-check in weekly follow-up; deploy-bot created the cadence. :thumbsup:

sophia: adding one more note — please include the cost impact estimate for the dedicated burst we used during the incident. ops/finance want a quick line item.

kevin: will add estimate to INF-4321 doc.

matt: any objections to closing the incident channel once all INF sub-tasks are scoped?

ana: no objections. keep this thread for quick async updates until the first follow-up check-in.

deploy-bot: Reminder scheduled for 1901300000 to validate INF-4321-2 alert firing.
